limits: Authors state the field is still in its infancy (Sec 10.3, 11).
No synthesis of benchmark scores across agents; the tables list benchmark size, metric and measurement, not results.
Does not state how papers were searched, selected or counted (no inclusion criteria, no PRISMA-style count); only 'over 500 references'.
Authors are Microsoft-affiliated; UFO and UFO2 are used as examples of multi-agent and picture-in-picture designs.
Several figures are described as conceptual or fabricated (Fig 30, Fig 31).
Benchmark numbers quoted are other work's and as of the cutoff of v12 (6 May 2025); OSWorld and other leaderboards have moved since.
practices: Prefer a hybrid agent: GUI operations for broad coverage, native APIs where available for efficiency (Sec 4.4).
Add screenshots to text inputs (DOM/HTML); the survey says visual input shows clear performance advantages (Sec 6.5).
Pure-vision agents need strong grounding; fine-tune for grounding or add GUI parsing such as OmniParser (Sec 6.5).
Use search or world-model methods (best-first, MCTS, WMA) for long-horizon web tasks (Sec 6.5).
Ask the user for manual login, disambiguation and explicit confirmation before irreversible actions such as sending email (Sec 11.4, Fig 31).
Add action validation, rollback, permission management and runtime safeguards (Sec 11.3).
Run inference on-device with compression, distillation and quantisation to address privacy and latency (Sec 11.1, 11.2).
Ask app developers to expose high-level native APIs that fold several UI operations into one call (Sec 11.2).
Give agents a knowledge base (docs, FAQs, demonstrations) and retrieve from it at runtime for unfamiliar apps (Sec 11.7).
Run the agent in a virtual desktop (picture-in-picture, UFO2) so it does not disturb the user's session (Sec 11.4).
Benchmarks should move to live environments, standardise a cross-platform interface, and add safety, privacy and compliance metrics (Sec 9.8).

terms.definition: Intelligent agents that operate within GUI environments, leveraging LLMs as their core inference and cognitive engine to generate, plan, and execute actions in a flexible and adaptive manner.
foundation LLMs fine-tuned with contextual, GUI-specific datasets to enhance their action-driven capabilities
ratio of the number of steps that are successful over the total steps within a task
successful task completion over all tasks set in the benchmark; ignores intermediate steps
ratio of turns that successfully address the request in that interaction over all turns
rate at which tasks are completed successfully while adhering to policy constraints
evaluates the potential risk associated with the agent's actions during task execution; lower is more trustworthy
Text Match, Image Match, Element Match, Action Match, State Information
